Definition: of foreign origin (H3801); a tunic or shirt:--clothes, coat, garment.
BiblicalUsage: Chiton is a tunic, the close garment worn under the outer robe, and the Gospels use it for generosity, for sharing and for the cross. Jesus says to give your coat as well as your cloak to the man who sues you, John the Baptist says the man with two coats should share with him who has none, and the soldiers gamble over the seamless coat of Jesus.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the coat in these sayings is the test of a generous heart, because it is the garment closest to the skin. I hold that Christ's seamless coat, gambled for at the cross, shows how far men will go to take what He wore.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
